(1) THE GUARD RESPELL at +0x8c-0x94. Target `cmpwi r0,0` + `mr r29,r0`; ours `extsh. r0,r3` + `addi r30,r3,0`. Two independent respells: our guard re-reads an s16 FIELD so MWCC re-extends (extsh.) where the target compares an already-int value (cmpwi), and our copy takes the `addi rD,rS,0` form where the target takes `mr`. Variant G closes the first and loses the second; no probed form closes both. This is the whole remaining count-exact gap and it is where the next lane should start.
(2) AN 8-BYTE DEAD REGION AT THE FRAME BOTTOM. Target's compiler-temp block (seven 4-byte bit-trick-abs slots) sits at 96..124; ours at 88..116. Neither stream references 8..96 / 8..88 at all. The target reserves 8 bytes more below the temp block than we do, and since declared locals are allocated ABOVE the temps, no declaration can reach it. Frames agree anyway because the target spends the difference on its sixth FPR. Candidate class: an unrecovered inlined callee's frame-bottom reservation.
(3) AN lfs SCHEDULE SWAP at +0x2cc/+0x2d8, one instruction, pure reorder. Source line `nv[1] = pos[1] - item->objgrp.coll_pos[1];`: the target issues the SUBTRAHEND load (`lfs f1,88(r25)`) three slots early, above the `cmpwi` belonging to the next statement's guard, then `fsubs f0,f0,f1`; ours loads pos[1] first and emits `fsubs f0,f1,f0`.
